question: Which of the following is the value of \(\sqrt{\log_2 6 + \log_3 6}?\)
solution:
Writing \(6=2\cdot3\) introduces the two logarithms appearing in choice D. Their reciprocal relationship will make the expression under the square root a perfect square.

Let
\[
a=\log_2 3,\qquad b=\log_3 2.
\]
Both are positive. By change of base,
\[
b=\frac{\log_2 2}{\log_2 3}=\frac1a,
\]
so \(ab=1\). The logarithm product rule gives
\[
\log_2 6+\log_3 6=(1+a)+(b+1)=a+b+2.
\]
On the other hand,
\[
(\sqrt a+\sqrt b)^2=a+b+2\sqrt{ab}=a+b+2.
\]
Since \(\sqrt a+\sqrt b\) is positive, it is the principal square root of this quantity. Therefore the value is
\[
\boxed{\sqrt{\log_2 3}+\sqrt{\log_3 2}},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

edges.reason: The source expressly permits an area interpretation of the perfect-square identity; polynomial multiplication is one derivation, not the only route to the stated formula-use criteria.

Contrasting the independent identities usefully prevents confusing a square of a sum with a product of a sum and difference. No learning order is necessary, but that misconception-prevention role supports preparation rather than mere thematic association.

The explicit reverse-use simplification extracts squared factors and uses sqrt(a squared)=|a| with the correct sign restriction.
